open_obligations: Check that book summarisation is beyond what a single human could evaluate in the relevant sense.
Note that only about 5% of summaries match human quality, so the demonstration is partial.
Confirm that Wu et al. use human feedback at every level rather than only at leaves.

Note that Wu et al. say only that their approach can be thought of as a specific instantiation of iterated amplification, with a fixed decomposition and training started from the leaf tasks rather than the entire tree, and that they fine-tune GPT-3 with behavioural cloning and reward modelling; check that it matches Iterated Amplification as Christiano et al. use the term before reading it as a test of their hypothesis.
in.other_title: Recursive task decomposition plus human feedback for summarizing entire books
in.rationale: Christiano et al. leave open whether Iterated Amplification can be usefully applied to complex real-world tasks for which no other training strategy is available. Wu et al. combine human feedback with recursive task decomposition to summarise whole books, report labelers could supervise without reading whole books, and find summaries match human quality in about 5% of books; at inference time the model summarises small sections and then recursively summarises those summaries. Wu et al. say their task decomposition approach can be thought of as a specific instantiation of iterated amplification, except that they assume a fixed decomposition and start training from the leaf tasks rather than using the entire tree, and that their contribution is showing the approach can be realistically applied to a difficult, large-scale task. The passages do not show whether the task is beyond what humans could evaluate directly or whether no other training strategy is available for it.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether Iterated Amplification can be usefully applied to complex real-world tasks for which no other training strategy is available, with Wu et al.'s whole-book summarisation by recursive task decomposition and human feedback as the candidate case
